description: Major philosophical traditions, thinkers, and questions in Western thought

branches_of_philosophy.metaphysics: Nature of reality; what exists and what it is like
branches_of_philosophy.epistemology: Nature of knowledge; how we know what we know
branches_of_philosophy.ethics: Moral principles; what is right and wrong
branches_of_philosophy.logic: Principles of valid reasoning and argument

pre_socratics.thales: First Greek philosopher; all is water
pre_socratics.heraclitus: All is flux; logos (reason) governs change; 'You can't step in the same river twice'
pre_socratics.parmenides: Reality is unchanging, eternal Being; change is illusion
pre_socratics.democritus: Atomism; matter made of indivisible atoms

socrates.method: Socratic method; elenchus; questioning to expose ignorance
socrates.key_idea: 'The unexamined life is not worth living'
socrates.fate: Sentenced to death for corrupting youth and impiety; chose hemlock

plato.theory_of_forms: Real world is world of eternal Forms; physical world is imperfect shadow
plato.ideal_state: Philosopher kings rule; guardians defend; producers work

aristotle.key_ideas: Empiricism; eudaimonia (flourishing) as goal; virtue ethics; four causes
aristotle.contribution: Founded logic, biology, physics, rhetoric as organized disciplines

descartes.key_idea: 'Cogito ergo sum' (I think, therefore I am)
descartes.method: Radical doubt; rebuild knowledge on certain foundations
descartes.dualism: Mind and body are distinct substances

locke.key_ideas: Tabula rasa (mind as blank slate); natural rights (life, liberty, property); social contract
locke.influence: American Declaration of Independence; liberal democracy

hume.key_ideas: Empiricism; skepticism about causation; 'is-ought' problem; miracles unlikely
hume.bundle_theory: Self is a bundle of perceptions, not a unified entity

kant.key_ideas: Categorical imperative; transcendental idealism; phenomena vs noumena
kant.categorical_imperative: Act only according to maxims you could will to be universal laws
works: Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals

19th_century.hegel: Dialectic (thesis-antithesis-synthesis); history as unfolding of Absolute Spirit
19th_century.mill: Utilitarianism; greatest happiness for greatest number; harm principle

nietzsche.key_ideas: Will to power; Übermensch (Overman); God is dead; eternal recurrence

19th_century.marx: Materialism; history as class struggle; communism; alienated labor

existentialism.core: Existence precedes essence; radical freedom and responsibility
existentialism.sartre: 'Hell is other people'; bad faith; being-in-itself vs being-for-itself
existentialism.camus: Absurdism; life has no inherent meaning but we must live fully anyway

analytic_philosophy.wittgenstein: Language games; limits of language are limits of world; Philosophical Investigations
analytic_philosophy.russell: Logical atomism; theory of descriptions; mathematical logic
analytic_philosophy.popper: Falsifiability as criterion of science; critical rationalism

postmodernism.foucault: Power/knowledge; genealogy of institutions; Discipline and Punish
